shots.picture: MEDIUM. The first bodyguard leans one big hand on the car's roof. **The car rocks on its stands, over the man underneath.** A stand scrapes. The legs stop.
UNDER THE CAR, close, the same frame as 0.5. The sump a hand above his face, still swaying. He doesn't look out. He doesn't raise his voice.
SAME FRAME as 0.8. The hand comes off the roof at once. Only then does the bodyguard look at Father. **Father has seen him do it.** He says nothing.
DOORWAY, held (v6, 23 Nov, decided): the bright street, the black car at the kerb, FATHER in the doorway, still. The guard has turned to him. No line: he has arrived.

HIGH, over Father's shoulder, looking down at the legs. The first bodyguard's sleeve holds the phone down towards them: **the one-star post**, and under it one big red button, **DELETE POST**, his thumb hovering over it. Father says nothing. The legs go on working: a clank.
UNDER THE CAR, close. The Client on his back, face lit by the lamp, working. He doesn't look out.

TWO-SHOT, the blue plan on the back wall (GARAGE 1–10, the tape, the bay 7 strip) and the second bodyguard, who has walked to it. His finger goes to one square: **GARAGE 7**. Then he looks round at the real bay they are standing in.
SAME FRAME. A gold lighter. CLICK: the flame, under the corner of GARAGE 7. The paper starts to brown. **Nobody says it.** The radio plays on.
WIDE, frame 0's frame. The creeper rolls out. The Client sits up on it, wipes his hands on a rag, looks at the flame, then **at his watch**.
CLOSE, the Client, to Father, flat, the rag still in his hands.
shots.line: CLIENT: "Burn them. Your son loses his only customer."

shots.picture: CLOSE, the bodyguard with the lighter, the loyal one. His sunglasses turn to Father for the order.
CLOSE, Father. **The left eyebrow goes up** (his one move in episode 12). A small shake of the head.
SAME FRAME as 1.2. CLICK: the lighter shuts. A brown mark on the corner of GARAGE 7 stays for the rest of the arc.
TWO-SHOT, Father and the Client, the car between them. Father speaks to him. **He has only ever spoken to Don.**
shots.line: FATHER: "My son says his machine finds anything."

shots.picture: CLOSE, the Client, back under the bonnet, not looking up.

SAME TWO-SHOT. Without looking, the Client holds the work lamp out behind him. The first bodyguard, the one who got off the car, takes it before anyone tells him to and holds it over the engine. **He is now a garage hand.**
CLOSE, Father, watching that. His man, holding a lamp for a mechanic. A long look. Then his eyes go from the lamp to the Client. **This is when he decides.**
CLOSE, Father, the bodyguard holding the lamp behind him.
shots.line: FATHER: "How would you run his company?"

shots.picture: CLOSE, the Client. He straightens up. Checks the watch.
CLOSE, Father. HELD, silent. He has just been asked to remove his son. He weighs it. Nothing on his face moves.
SAME FRAME. Business.
MEDIUM. The Client takes his phone out of his top pocket, wipes the screen on his trousers, turns it round.
INSERT, the phone, held out to Father, filling the frame: one contact card, nothing else on screen. **PAM — finds things.** (He saved it in episode 11.)
CLOSE, the Client, phone still held out. His terms from episode 9, now for her.
shots.line: CLIENT: "One month. I ask. She finds it."

shots.picture: TWO-SHOT. Father nods once. That is all.
MEDIUM, the car. The Client drops the bonnet: SLAM. Wipes it once with the rag where his hand was.
INSERT, the ignition, his oily fingers on the key. It turns. The engine coughs, then catches and runs, smooth: **he fixed it.** The radio is drowned for a moment.
CLOSE, the first bodyguard, still holding the work lamp over a shut bonnet. Nothing left to light. He keeps holding it.
MEDIUM. Father, without turning his head, to the loyal bodyguard. The bodyguard thumbs his phone: a calendar entry.
EXT, UptimeZ Inc.: the glass doors, the logo, the lobby lit. The calendar chime.

HARD CUT. THE FRONT DESK, wide, the set from episode 10. Don on the throne, feet up, the crown behind his head. The robot at its station by the door. Pam at the counter. Sofía is not in this episode. A cheerful **chime**.
CLOSE, the robot. Its visor: a calendar card, one line big enough to read on a phone: **WITHOUT HIM**. Delighted.
CLOSE, Don on the throne, the crown behind his head. He has sat up for good news. The smile stays on.
CLOSE, the robot. **ITS HEAD TURNS, SLOWLY**, to Don (the move from episode 12). Still smiling. Says nothing. **The peak: hold it.**
CLOSE, the robot, turned to Don, smiling.
CLOSE, Don, the same frame as 3.3. He follows the robot's look down, to himself. The smile goes in one drawing.
CLOSE, Don, turning to the counter.
CLOSE, Pam (v7, 23 Nov, decided: held 2.6 s). Buzz; her glasses come down onto her nose; INVITATION from FATHER, readable; a small smile: she knows; her eyes to Don, held; back; the phone face down.
CLOSE, the robot: its visor counts down. MEETING IN 4:59.
CLOSE, Don. He calls DAD. It rings. And rings. Nobody answers. The sweat comes back.
(v8, 23 Nov, cold tests 3 of 3) Father in the doorway, DONNIE buzzing in his hand, he looks at it (0.9 s); CLOSE: his thumb on red, DECLINED, face down.

HARD CUT. **FRAME 0'S DRAWING**: the bay, the car on stands, the legs on the creeper, the lamp on the floor, the radio, nobody else. The only difference from frame 0: **the brown burn mark on GARAGE 7** on the plan (as episode 10's loop differs only by the calendar). The engine outside pulls away. Cut to 0.1: the loop.
